metadata.purpose: Evidence-aware starter knowledge base for a household-observation soil assessment prototype.
limitations: Household checks are screening observations, not laboratory diagnoses.
Do not diagnose sodicity or salinity from one visual sign.
Do not prescribe fixed amendment doses or heavy flushing when drainage or water quality is unknown.
Survivor-facing checks must use eyes, hands, and household items, without instruments, lab readings, or fixed scientific thresholds.
Crop-specific advice must be verified for the local climate and growing conditions before being presented as a strong recommendation.

assessment_categories.label: Possible sodium-affected soil
assessment_categories.meaning: Evidence may suggest unstable soil structure associated with sodium, but does not confirm sodicity.

assessment_categories.label: Possible salinity concern
assessment_categories.meaning: Observations may suggest salt accumulation, but visual residue alone cannot establish soil salinity.

assessment_categories.label: Possible heavy clay or compaction
assessment_categories.meaning: Poor infiltration may relate to texture, compaction, surface sealing, drainage, or mixed causes.

assessment_categories.label: Mixed evidence or insufficient information
assessment_categories.meaning: Available observations do not support one defensible explanation.

knowledge_records.title: Sodicity can damage soil structure
knowledge_records.fact: Excess sodium associated with the soil exchange complex can contribute to clay dispersion and degraded soil physical properties, including poor infiltration.
knowledge_records.use_in_reasoning: Treat dispersion-like observations as a clue that may support a sodium-related concern, not as confirmation.
limitations: Household observations cannot measure exchangeable sodium or confirm sodicity.

knowledge_records.title: Salinity and sodicity differ
knowledge_records.fact: Saline and sodic soils have different characteristics and can require different management strategies.
knowledge_records.use_in_reasoning: Keep possible salinity and possible sodicity as separate interpretations.
limitations: The distinction cannot be confirmed from appearance alone.

knowledge_records.title: Poor infiltration has multiple possible causes
knowledge_records.fact: Water ponding and surface crusting do not, by themselves, establish that sodium or soluble salts are the cause.
knowledge_records.use_in_reasoning: Consider heavy clay, compaction, surface sealing, drainage constraints, sodicity, or mixed causes.
limitations: Further evidence may be needed to distinguish the cause.

knowledge_records.title: Moist soil squeeze or ribbon check
knowledge_records.purpose: Explore whether moist soil behaves like clay-rich soil.
procedure: Moisten a small sample gradually until workable, not runny.
Squeeze and roll it gently between fingers.
Observe whether it holds together and whether a ribbon can form.
knowledge_records.possible_interpretation: Soil that moulds readily or forms a ribbon may contain substantial clay.
cannot_prove: Drainage performance across the whole plot
knowledge_records.next_step: Combine with the crumb-in-water and drainage observations.

knowledge_records.title: Dry soil crumb in still water
knowledge_records.purpose: Observe whether a dry soil crumb stays intact or disperses in still water.
procedure: Place a small dry crumb gently in still water.
Observe whether it mostly holds together, breaks apart, or makes the water cloudy.
knowledge_records.possible_interpretation: Visible dispersion may support concern about unstable soil structure and a possible sodium-related problem.
knowledge_records.next_step: Combine with other observations; if unclear, report uncertainty.

knowledge_records.title: Dig-and-fill drainage observation
knowledge_records.purpose: Observe whether water enters the soil or remains ponded.
procedure: Dig a small hole if it is safe to do so.
Add a bucketful of water and observe whether it drains or remains standing.
Do not treat one observation as a precise infiltration measurement.
knowledge_records.possible_interpretation: Persistent standing water suggests a water-entry or drainage concern.
cannot_prove: That the entire plot behaves the same way
knowledge_records.next_step: Avoid prolonged ponding; consider safe surface drainage and seek local advice if water remains standing.
knowledge_records.safety_note: Do not dig where buried utilities, unstable ground, or other hazards may be present.

knowledge_records.title: Water evaporation on a dark plate
knowledge_records.purpose: Look for residue after a small amount of water evaporates.
procedure: Put a small spoonful of water on a clean dark plate.
Let it evaporate naturally in a safe place.
knowledge_records.possible_interpretation: Residue may indicate dissolved material in the water sample.
cannot_prove: That the residue is a particular salt
Whether the water is safe for irrigation
knowledge_records.safety_note: Do not taste the water or residue. Keep the plate away from food preparation and children.
knowledge_records.next_step: Treat water quality as unknown without reliable evidence; do not recommend flushing based on this check alone.

knowledge_records.title: Organic matter
knowledge_records.general_guidance: Suitable mature compost or clean plant residues may help build soil organic matter and support soil structure over time.
conditions: Avoid working wet clay if it would smear or compact.
limitations: Organic matter alone does not prove or fully correct sodicity.
Improvement may take more than one growing season.

knowledge_records.title: Surface mulch
knowledge_records.general_guidance: A suitable layer of clean plant mulch can protect the soil surface from direct impact and rapid drying.
conditions: Use material suitable for the crop and local conditions.
limitations: Mulch does not diagnose or independently correct sodicity and may not solve ponding.

knowledge_records.title: Calcium-rich amendment requires evidence
knowledge_records.general_guidance: Calcium-rich amendments such as gypsum are used in some sodic-soil management plans, but suitability and amount depend on soil and water conditions.
conditions: Do not prescribe a fixed amount from visual signs alone.
Do not recommend automatically for ordinary compacted clay.
Consider drainage and how displaced salts would be managed.
limitations: The household workflow cannot calculate a reliable amendment requirement.
Local agricultural advice may be needed.

knowledge_records.title: Do not automatically flush soil
knowledge_records.general_guidance: Avoid recommending heavy or repeated flushing when drainage is poor or irrigation-water quality is unknown.
conditions: The cause of the soil problem is uncertain.
limitations: This is a conservative safety gate, not a complete reclamation prescription.

knowledge_records.title: Crop suggestions must be conditional
knowledge_records.general_guidance: Offer multiple crop candidates only after considering soil condition, drainage, water availability, climate, and locally suitable varieties.
conditions: Do not equate salt tolerance with tolerance of prolonged waterlogging.
Explain remaining risks and let the user choose.
Verify maturity ranges and tolerance from a suitable local source.
limitations: A universal crop list is intentionally not included until local conditions and crop-specific evidence are verified.

knowledge_records.title: Care by growth stage
knowledge_records.general_guidance: Organize care into establishment, vegetative growth, reproductive stage, and harvest; check for wilting, crusting, standing water, nutrient problems, and disease symptoms.
conditions: Adapt actions to the selected crop.
Do not automatically add water when soil is already ponded.
limitations: Crop-specific intervals and treatments must be verified before use.

knowledge_records.title: Harvest and protect soil structure
knowledge_records.general_guidance: Use crop-specific visible maturity signs, harvest appropriately, and where safe return clean plant residues to support organic matter.
conditions: Do not return diseased or contaminated residues without guidance.
Avoid working heavy clay when wet enough to smear or compact.
limitations: Ripeness signs and harvest methods depend on the selected crop.

if: Required observations are missing or contradictory
reasoning_rules.explanation: Do not fill gaps with invented observations.

if: Water remains ponded or drainage appears poor
reasoning_rules.explanation: Water management must be considered alongside soil repair.

if: Dry crumb visibly disperses in still water

then.action: Explain that unstable structure is a clue and gather additional evidence

reasoning_rules.explanation: A household crumb check is suggestive, not definitive.

if: White residue is observed after water evaporates

then.action: Explain the limitation and investigate water/soil context

reasoning_rules.explanation: Residue may come from dissolved material and does not prove soil salinity.

avoid: Recommending heavy flushing based only on visual checks

reasoning_rules.explanation: The plate check cannot determine irrigation-water safety.

if: Sodicity is not adequately supported by available evidence

then.action: Do not prescribe gypsum or another calcium-rich amendment automatically

reasoning_rules.explanation: Amendment choice and amount depend on the underlying soil and water conditions.

readiness_gate.title: Before planting or intensifying irrigation
proceed_when: Relevant available household checks have been completed.
Water is not persistently ponded in the intended planting area.
Surface condition and soil-crumb observations have been reviewed together.
Water quality is understood well enough for the proposed use, or uncertainty is clearly flagged.
Any amendment recommendation is supported by appropriate evidence or local expert guidance.
pause_or_reassess_when: Water remains standing after the drainage observation.
The crumb check and other observations conflict.
Water source quality is unknown and the proposed action depends on it.
The system would need to guess an amendment type or quantity.
Evidence does not distinguish possible sodicity, salinity, and ordinary compaction.
